Here's an example query:
```
SELECT column_name, COUNT(*) as count
FROM table_name
GROUP BY column_name
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
```
This query will count the number of unique values in each column of the `table_name` table and filter out groups that have more than one value.

In this guide, we will walk you through the process of uploading a bibliography database to Overleaf, including creating an account, installing the Overleaf package, creating a new document, adding references using the Overleaf package, and deploying the document to the Overleaf platform.

Step 1: Creating an Overleaf Account

1. Go to the Overleaf website (<https://www.overleaf.com/>) and click on "Sign Up" in the top right corner.
2. Enter your email address, choose a password, and provide a name for your account.
3. Click "Create Account" to sign up for an Overleaf account.

Step 2: Installing the Overleaf Package

1. Open your preferred text editor (e.g., Google Docs, Microsoft Word, Sublime Text).
2. Search for "Overleaf" in the package manager or extension library of your text editor.
3. Install the Overleaf package by following the in-app instructions.
4. Once the package is installed, open the Overleaf menu in your text editor and select "New Document" to create a new Overleaf document.

Step 3: Creating a New Document

1. In your text editor, select "New Document" from the Overleaf menu.
2. Choose the desired document type (e.g., LaTeX, Markdown, HTML).
3. Enter a title and description for your document, and select the appropriate template.
4. Click "Create Document" to create a new Overleaf document.

Step 4: Adding References Using the Overleaf Package

1. In your Overleaf document, click on the "References" button in the top menu bar.
2. Select the citation style you want to use (e.g., APA, MLA, Chicago).
3. Enter the details of your references in the appropriate fields, such as author, title, and publication date.
4. Use the "Add Citation" button to add each reference to your bibliography.

Step 5: Deploying the Document to the Overleaf Platform

1. Once you have completed your document, click on the "Deploy" button in the top menu bar.
2. Choose the desired deployment option (e.g., PDF, LaTeX, HTML).
3. Enter the desired file name and description for your deployment.
4. Click "Deploy" to deploy your document to the Overleaf platform.

Tips and Tricks:

* Overleaf offers a range of templates and styles to help you get started with your document.
* You can collaborate with others in real-time by inviting them to edit your document.
* Overleaf provides a range of tools and features to help you manage and organize your bibliography, including automatic citation formatting and the ability to import references from external sources.
* You can easily share your document with others by generating a shareable link or downloading it as a PDF, LaTeX, or HTML file.

Conclusion:
In this guide, we have covered the steps for uploading a bibliography database to Overleaf, including creating an account, installing the Overleaf package, creating a new document, adding references using the Overleaf package, and deploying the document to the Overleaf platform. By following these steps, you can easily create and manage your bibliography on Overleaf, a powerful and collaborative platform for document creation and sharing.

It's important to approach the situation in a sensitive and respectful manner to avoid any further conflict or hurt feelings. Here are some suggestions on how to handle the situation:

1. Have an open and honest conversation: It's important to talk to your friend directly and express your feelings in a non-accusatory way. Choose a private and comfortable setting where you both feel safe and comfortable sharing your thoughts. Be honest about how their behavior is affecting you and your trip, but also be sure to listen to their perspective and understand their point of view.

This can help avoid blame and defensiveness and can help your friend understand your perspective better. For example, "I feel really frustrated when you don't want to talk to me or engage in activities. I'm here to enjoy this trip with you, but I feel like I can't do that when you're not participating."

context: Ten European football teams – the Netherlands, England, Belgium, Denmark, France, Germany, Norway, Sweden, Switzerland and Wales – will participate in a season-long “OneLove” campaign promoting inclusion and opposing discrimination.
expected_response:
Every country except Sweden and Norway has qualified for the 2022 World Cup in Qatar and each captain of these eight nations will wear a distinctive OneLove armband – which features a heart containing colors from all backgrounds – during the tournament.
The Netherlands FA, which is spearheading the campaign, chose the colors to represent all heritages, backgrounds, genders and sexual identities; the armband will be worn in Qatar where same-sex relationships are a criminal offense.
Sweden and Norway will participate in the initiative during the upcoming Nations League matches, while England will also wear black armbands during both its UEFA Nations League matches to mark the death of Queen Elizabeth II.
“This is an important message which suits the game of football: on the field everybody is equal and this should be the case in every place in society. With the OneLove band we express this message,” said Virgil van Dijk, the Netherlands captain.
“On behalf of the Dutch team I have been wearing this band for quite a while now. It is good to see that other countries are joining this initiative.”
OneLove was founded in the Netherlands in 2020 to emphasize that all football fans have at least one thing in common – their love of football – and to speak out against any form of discrimination.
As well as focusing on public messaging, the initiative has also developed to offer diversity training to grassroots club.
“Our love of football unites us all. No matter where you come from, what you look like and who you love. Football is there for everyone and our sport must stand up for the people across the world who face discrimination and exclusion,” said Germany captain Manuel Neuer.
“I am proud to be sending out this message with my colleagues from the other national teams. Every single voice counts.”
In June, England’s captain Harry Kane revealed that he had discussed taking a collective stance regarding human rights in Qatar with Denmark’s Christian Eriksen and France captain Hugo Lloris.
“I am honored to join my fellow national team captains in supporting the important OneLove campaign,” he said on Tuesday.
“As captains we may all be competing against each other on the pitch, but we stand together against all forms of discrimination. This is even more relevant at a time when division is common in society. Wearing the armband together on behalf of our teams will send a clear message when the world is watching.”

Section Title: Trusty Jeans - The Ultimate Travel Companion

Overview:
Jeans are a staple in every traveler's wardrobe, and for good reason. They are versatile, comfortable, and can be dressed up or down to suit any occasion. In this section, we'll explore the reasons why jeans are a must-have for your next trip, and provide tips on how to style them for maximum comfort and fashion.

Why Jeans are a Travel Essential:

* Versatility: Jeans can be worn in a variety of settings, from casual outings to more formal events. They can be dressed up with a nice blouse or blazer, or dressed down with a t-shirt and sneakers.
* Comfort: Jeans are made from stretchy material that provides maximum comfort, making them perfect for long days of sightseeing or exploring.
* Durability: Jeans are built to last, and can withstand the rigors of travel without losing their shape or form.

How to Style Jeans for Travel:

* Layering: Layering is key to styling jeans for travel. Try pairing a lightweight denim jacket with a t-shirt and sneakers for a casual look, or layering a blazer over a dressy top and jeans for a more formal occasion.
* Mix and Match: Don't be afraid to mix and match different styles of jeans to create a unique look. For example, try pairing a distressed denim jacket with a flowy sundress for a bohemian-inspired look.
* Accessorize: Add a pop of color or personality to your outfit with accessories like scarves, hats, or jewelry.

Tips for Traveling with Jeans:

* Pack a few pairs: While you may think you can get by with just one pair of jeans, trust us, you'll want to have a few options. Pack a few pairs in different washes and styles to ensure you have the perfect pair for every occasion.
* Roll them up: To save space in your luggage, try rolling your jeans instead of folding them. This will help prevent wrinkles and creases.
* Use a jean steamer: If you're worried about your jeans getting wrinkled during travel, consider investing in a portable jean steamer. This will help keep your jeans looking fresh and wrinkle-free.

Conclusion:
Jeans are a versatile and essential item to include in your travel wardrobe. With their comfort, durability, and versatility, they can be dressed up or down to suit any occasion. By following the tips outlined in this section, you'll be able to style your jeans for maximum comfort and fashion, and enjoy your next trip with confidence.

ori_prompt: Write a step-by-step guide for resolving GitHub merge conflicts.
expected_response:
1- Under your repository name, click Pull requests.
2- In the "Pull Requests" list, click the pull request with a merge conflict that you'd like to resolve.
3- Near the bottom of your pull request, click Resolve conflicts.
4- Decide if you want to keep only your branch's changes, keep only the other branch's changes, or make a brand new change, which may incorporate changes from both branches. Delete the conflict markers <<<<<<<, =======, >>>>>>> and make the changes you want in the final merge.
5- If you have more than one merge conflict in your file, scroll down to the next set of conflict markers and repeat steps four and five to resolve your merge conflict.
6- Once you've resolved all the conflicts in the file, click Mark as resolved.
7- If you have more than one file with a conflict, select the next file you want to edit on the left side of the page under "conflicting files" and repeat steps four through seven until you've resolved all of your pull request's merge conflicts.
8- Once you've resolved all your merge conflicts, click Commit merge. This merges the entire base branch into your head branch.
9- If prompted, review the branch that you are committing to.
If the head branch is the default branch of the repository, you can choose either to update this branch with the changes you made to resolve the conflict, or to create a new branch and use this as the head branch of the pull request.
If you choose to create a new branch, enter a name for the branch.
If the head branch of your pull request is protected you must create a new branch. You won't get the option to update the protected branch.
Click Create branch and update my pull request or I understand, continue updating BRANCH. The button text corresponds to the action you are performing.
10- To merge your pull request, click Merge pull request. For more information about other pull request merge options, see "Merging a pull request."

Step 1: Understand the Conflict

* When you try to merge two branches in GitHub, the platform will detect conflicts and display them in a conflict message.
* The conflict message will highlight the lines of code that have conflicts and provide a brief description of the conflict.
* Take a moment to review the conflict message and understand the nature of the conflict.

Step 2: Open the Conflict File

* Open the file that has the conflict using a text editor or the GitHub desktop application.
* The file will have a `.diff` extension, which indicates that it contains the differences between the two branches.
* Review the conflicts in the file, paying attention to the line numbers and the changes made in each branch.

Step 3: Resolve the Conflict

* Review the conflicts one by one, and determine which changes to keep and which to discard.
* You can use the following strategies to resolve conflicts:
	+ Keep the changes from the latest commit: If the conflict is between two changes made in the same commit, you can keep the changes from the latest commit.
	+ Keep the changes from the other branch: If the conflict is between changes made in different commits, you can keep the changes from the other branch.
	+ Revert the changes: If you cannot resolve the conflict, you can revert the changes by selecting the revert option in the conflict message.
* Once you have resolved the conflicts, save the file and close the text editor or GitHub desktop application.

Step 4: Commit the Resolved Conflict

* After resolving the conflicts, you need to commit the changes to the repository.
* Open a terminal or the GitHub desktop application and navigate to the repository.
* Run the following command to commit the changes:
```
git add <file name>
git commit -m "Resolved conflicts"
```
* Replace `<file name>` with the name of the file that has conflicts.
* The commit message should describe the changes made to resolve the conflicts.

Step 5: Merge the Branches

* After committing the resolved conflicts, you can merge the branches.
* Open a terminal or the GitHub desktop application and navigate to the repository.
* Run the following command to merge the branches:
```
git merge <branch name>
```
* Replace `<branch name>` with the name of the branch you want to merge.
* The merge will automatically apply the changes from the other branch to your current branch.

Step 6: Review the Merge

* After merging the branches, review the changes to ensure that they are correct.
* You can use the `git log` command to view the commit history and check the changes made during the merge.
* If necessary, you can undo the merge by running the `git reset` command.

* Conflicts can occur when two developers make changes to the same line of code.
* Conflicts can also occur when the changes are made in different commits, and the platform cannot automatically resolve the conflicts.
* If you encounter any issues during the conflict resolution process, you can try the following:
	+ Check the commit history to identify the changes made in each commit.
	+ Use the `git status` command to view the changes made in the repository.
	+ Reach out to your team members to resolve the conflicts.

By following these steps, you can effectively identify and resolve merge conflicts in a GitHub repository, ensuring that your changes are properly merged and your repository remains in a stable state.

To answer your first question, multiprocessing offers several advantages over threading:

1. Resource sharing: In multiprocessing, each process has its own memory space, which means that processes can't directly access each other's memory. This can be useful for protecting sensitive data or avoiding race conditions.
2. Scalability: Multiprocessing can handle more concurrent tasks than threading, as each process can run in parallel, whereas threads within a process share the same memory space and can interfere with each other.
3. Flexibility: Multiprocessing allows you to run different tasks in different processes, which can be useful for tasks that require different environments or dependencies.

However, threading can also be useful in certain scenarios, such as:

1. Inter-process communication: Threading can be used to communicate between processes, which can be more efficient than using inter-process communication mechanisms like queues or pipes.
2. Lightweight processes: Threads are lighterweight than processes, which means they can be created and destroyed more quickly and use less memory.

Objective: Write a function in Python that finds the optimal subarray sum of a given array using dynamic programming.

Examples:

* Input: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
* Output: 15 (the optimal subarray sum is [1, 2, 3, 4])
* Input: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]

```
def optimal_subarray_sum(arr):

    dp = [0] * (n + 1)
    dp[0] = arr[0]

    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        for j in range(i):
            dp[i] = arr[j] + dp[j + 1]

    return dp[n]
```

Finally, the function returns the optimal subarray sum, which is the maximum value of the subarray sum for any subarray of the input array.

Finally! After a while of shooting in the dark and frantically fiddling with sample inputs on the whiteboard, you've came up with an algorithm for solving the coding question your interviewer gave you.
Whew. Such a relief to have a clear path forward. To not be flailing anymore.
Now you're cruising, getting ready to code up your solution.
When suddenly, your interviewer throws you a curve ball.
"What if we thought of the problem this way?"
You feel a tension we've all felt during the coding interview:
"Try to listen to what they're saying...but don't lose your train of thought...ugh, I can't do both!"
expected_response:
Your interviewer probably won't fault you for going down the wrong path at first. They've seen really smart engineers do the same thing. They understand it's because you only have a partial view of the maze.
They might have let you go down the wrong path for a bit to see if you could keep your thinking organized without help. But now they want to rush you through the part where you discover the dead end and double back. Not because they don't believe you can manage it yourself. But because they want to make sure you have enough time to finish the question.
But here's something they will fault you for: failing to listen to them. Nobody wants to work with an engineer who doesn't listen.
So when you find yourself in that crucial coding interview moment, when you're torn between holding your train of thought and considering the idea your interviewer is suggesting...remember this:
Listening to your interviewer is the most important thing.
Take what they're saying and run with it. Think of the next steps that follow from what they're saying.

The "fair trade" movement, also known as the "trade justice" movement, is a social and economic movement that promotes the use of labor, environmental, and social standards for the production of commodities, particularly those exported from the Third and Second Worlds to the First World. The movement emerged in the 1960s and 1970s as a response to the exploitative practices of multinational corporations and the unequal global trade system.

The core principles of fair trade are:

1. Fair prices: Fair trade ensures that producers in developing countries receive a fair price for their products, which is higher than the market price and reflects the true value of their work.
2. Labor standards: Fair trade promotes safe and healthy working conditions, as well as the rights of workers to organize and bargain collectively.
3. Environmental standards: Fair trade promotes sustainable agriculture and forestry practices, and reduces the use of harmful chemicals and pesticides.
4. Social standards: Fair trade promotes social justice and equality, and supports the rights of marginalized groups, such as women and indigenous peoples.

The fair trade movement has gained significant momentum in recent years, with many consumers and businesses choosing to buy fair trade products as a way to support ethical and sustainable trade practices. However, the movement has also sparked a debate on whether trade itself should be codified as a human right.

Codifying trade as a human right would recognize the fundamental right of all individuals and communities to access fair and equitable trade opportunities. This would involve the establishment of a framework that ensures that trade is conducted in a way that promotes social, economic, and environmental justice, and that respects the rights and dignity of all parties involved.

There are several arguments in favor of codifying trade as a human right:

1. Promoting economic justice: Codifying trade as a human right would help to address the unequal distribution of wealth and resources that exists in the global economy. It would ensure that all individuals and communities have access to fair and equitable trade opportunities, regardless of their location or socio-economic status.
2. Protecting the environment: The fair trade movement has shown that it is possible to produce goods and services in a sustainable and environmentally-friendly way. 1. Creativity: Social media marketers need to be creative in developing innovative and engaging content that resonates with their target audience. They should be able to think outside the box and come up with unique ideas that set their brand apart from the competition.

Example: A social media marketer who creates a viral video campaign that showcases their brand's personality and values, while also resonating with their target audience, demonstrates strong creativity.

2. Strategic thinking: Social media marketers need to have a strategic mindset when developing their campaigns. They should be able to identify their target audience, set clear goals, and develop a plan to achieve those goals.

Example: A social media marketer who creates a comprehensive social media strategy that aligns with their brand's overall marketing goals, and includes specific tactics to engage their target audience, demonstrates strong strategic thinking.

3. Attention to detail: Social media marketers need to be detail-oriented when creating and managing their campaigns. They should be able to identify and correct errors, and ensure that their content is consistent and high-quality.

Example: A social media marketer who carefully crafts each social media post, ensuring that the visuals, copy, and hashtags are all aligned with their brand's messaging and goals, demonstrates strong attention to detail.

4. Communication skills: Social media marketers need to be effective communicators, both in writing and verbally. They should be able to articulate their brand's message and values, and engage with their audience in a way that builds trust and loyalty.

Example: A social media marketer who crafts compelling social media posts that effectively communicate their brand's message, and who is able to respond to customer inquiries and comments in a timely and professional manner, demonstrates strong communication skills.

Example: A social media marketer who is able to adjust their content strategy to align with changes in their brand's messaging, or who is able to pivot to a new platform or tactic when it becomes clear that it will be more effective, demonstrates strong adaptability.

They should be able to use tools such as Google Analytics and social media insights to track their progress and identify areas for improvement.

Example: A social media marketer who uses data to identify which types of content are most effective for their brand, and who adjusts their strategy accordingly, demonstrates strong data analysis skills.

Example: A social media marketer who works closely with the content marketing team to develop a cohesive content strategy, and who collaborates with the PR team to leverage social media for media coverage, demonstrates strong collaboration skills.

1- DAY 1: MARRAKECH
Arrive in time to meet your fellow travelers for a welcome gathering this evening. Your arrival transfer is included.
2- DAY 2: MARRAKECH/OUARZAZATE
Wind past red slopes and green terraces as we make our way south through the stunning valleys of Morocco’s High Atlas Mountains, stopping to enjoy a picnic lunch beside a sparkling river. Arrive in Ouarzazate, known as the “gateway to the Sahara,” and step behind the scenes at a film studio to see how the surrounding dunes have starred on the silver screen.
3- DAY 3: OUARZAZATE/MERZOUGA
Today, travel between jagged peaks and palm oases toward the desert town of Merzouga. Settle into our hotel near the incredible Erg Chebbi, a sweeping sea of dunes formed by wind-blown sand. As the sun sets, savour a traditional Amazigh dinner, then spread a blanket on the sand for an evening of desert stargazing.
4- DAY 4: MERZOUGA
This morning, hop aboard a 4x4 and ride across the dunes to discover fossils left behind by an ancient sea, and be entranced by Gnaoua musicians in a local village. Return to the hotel for free time to cool off in the pool. Enjoy a tasty Amazigh dinner, then gather around a glowing bonfire for a storytelling session.
5- DAY 5: MERZOUGA/DADES GORGE
Venture into the rugged landscape of the Dades Gorge, a dramatic and colourful valley carved by the waters of the Dades River. Visit a local village for lunch and enjoy a special dish—traditional Amazigh pizza! Wind through the valley on a guided walk as you learn about the amazing geology behind the weird and wonderful rock formations of the Gorge. This evening, enjoy free time to relax at the hotel.
6- DAY 6: DADES GORGE/AÏT BEN HADDOU
Drive through the Ounila Valley to the ancient fortified village of Aït Ben Haddou, a UNESCO World Heritage site where clay houses crowd together in a traditional ksar behind defensive walls. Explore alleyways twisting between historic structures, and stand guard atop the clay brick ramparts, taking in views of the green oasis around this imposing fort. Entertain your taste buds at a hands-on tagine cooking class, followed by a delicious dinner.
7- DAY 7: AÏT BEN HADDOU/MARRAKECH
Journey through the mountains to Marrakech, known as the “red city” for its walls, houses, and many mosques built from red clay. After checking into your hotel and resting up, head to a local henna workshop to have your hands painted in this ancient temporary tattooing art. Then, explore the lively Djemaa el Fna, an ancient marketplace still used as the main square in Marrakech. After, enjoy free time to discover more of Marrakech.
8- DAY 8: MARRAKECH 
Wake up as the call to prayer echoes across the city. After breakfast, set out on a guided walk through the narrow, maze-like streets of the medina, lined with colorful shops brimming with rugs, spices, and much more. Spend the rest of the day exploring Marrakech on your own, or opt to explore the Marjorelle Garden. In the evening, gather for a farewell dinner in a traditional riad, a grand house with an elegant interior courtyard.
9- DAY 9: MARRAKECH
Depart at any time.

rmepo_prompt: Provide specific strategies for students to effectively manage and reduce nervousness when delivering class presentations.
bpo_response:
Certainly! Here are some tips and strategies that can help students manage their nerves during class presentations:

1. Practice, practice, practice: The more you practice your presentation, the more confident you will feel. Practice in front of a mirror, family members, or friends to get used to speaking in front of an audience.
2. Prepare thoroughly: Make sure you know your material inside out. Research your topic and organize your thoughts before the presentation. This will help you feel more confident and in control.
3. Take deep breaths: Before you start your presentation, take a few deep breaths to calm your nerves. This can help slow down your heart rate and reduce any physical symptoms of anxiety.
4. Focus on your message: Instead of worrying about how you're coming across, focus on the message you're trying to convey. Remember, you're presenting the information to share knowledge and ideas, not to impress the audience.
5. Visualize success: Imagine yourself delivering a successful presentation and receiving positive feedback from the audience. Visualizing success can help boost your confidence and reduce nerves.
6. Use positive self-talk: Instead of telling yourself you're going to fail or that you're not good enough, try using positive affirmations. Tell yourself that you're well-prepared and that you're going to do a great job.
7. Use body language to your advantage: Make eye contact, stand up straight, and use appropriate gestures to convey confidence and authority. Avoid fidgeting, crossing your arms, or leaning on the podium.
8. Speak slowly and clearly: Avoid rushing through your presentation. Speak slowly and clearly, pausing for emphasis and to allow your audience to absorb the information.
9. Engage with your audience: Make eye contact, ask questions, and encourage audience participation. This can help you connect with your audience and distract you from your nerves.
10. Learn relaxation techniques: Consider learning relaxation techniques such as progressive muscle relaxation, visualization, or meditation to help manage your nerves before and during the presentation.

Remember, it's normal to feel some level of nervousness when presenting in front of an audience. However, with practice and preparation, you can learn to manage your nerves and deliver a confident and effective presentation.

expected_response:
This power booster recycles a 'dead' battery to power a 1.8 volt red LED light. It's mainly made from recycled parts.
When a 1.5 volt battery is new it will probably have more than 1.5 volts in it. As the battery is used the voltage will decrease until the voltage is not enough to run the application ( E.g. a red LED) and will be called 'dead' . But a Dead battery still has some power remaining in it - just not enough voltage. The trick is to use some of that remaining power to increase the voltage in a circuit. The trade off being there will be a reduction in current.
Here is the required steps:
1- Connect a switch to a battery holder. A soldiering iron and hot glue gun assisted with this.
2- Make a small pyramid above the battery holder using 4 bamboo skewer sticks secured with hot glue.
3- Soldier on a 1.8 volt red LED at the top of the mini Christmas tree.
4- Test the LED glows with a new battery (1.6 volts)
5- Test the LED doesn't glow with a dead battery (1.2 volts)
6- Add in the buzzer circuit, along with a switch.
7- Add in the windings circuit - to touch the striker of the buzzer a little copper foil was added.
8- Insert a dead battery (1.2 volt) with the buzzer circuit turned switch off - the LED will not glow but when the buzzer circuit is switched on the Red LED lights up.

Project Title: "Upcycled Electronic Art Installation"

Concept: Take old, broken, or obsolete electronic devices and transform them into a unique and visually striking art installation. The installation could be a sculpture, a mosaic, or a light installation, and could be displayed in a gallery or exhibited outdoors.

Materials:

* Old electronic devices (e.g. computers, phones, tablets, printers, etc.)
* Wiring and cables
* Wood or other materials for the base or structure of the installation
* Adhesives and fasteners (e.g. hot glue, epoxy, screws, etc.)
* LED lights or other lighting elements
* Power source (e.g. batteries, a power strip, etc.)

Steps to Develop the Idea:

1. Gather materials: Collect a variety of old electronic devices and sort them by type and condition. Look for items that are in good working condition but no longer needed or wanted.
2. Clean and prepare the materials: Clean the devices thoroughly and remove any hazardous components (e.g. batteries, circuit boards, etc.). Remove any unnecessary parts or components that are not needed for the installation.
3. Design the installation: Sketch out a rough design for the installation, taking into account the size and shape of the space where it will be displayed. Consider the color scheme, texture, and overall aesthetic you want to achieve.

expected_response:
Step 1: Close Drink Opening
To build up steam the beverage can needs to act as a pressure vessel and so needs to be completely sealed, except where the steam will come out of the jet nozzles. It also needs to rotate on itself. Bend up the outer tab into a L shape using some pilers and then bend it forward so a piece of string can hang from it over the center of the can. This will allow the can to rotate on itself. Close the pouring opening by using a knife or other thin object, bending the opening back up so it almost where it was before the beverage can was opened.
Step 2: Nozzel Jets
Make a couple of holes in the side of the can, about half way up, opposite each other using a small drill. The diameter of the holes should be about the same as the thin plastic tubing to be used as jet nozzles. Enlarge the holes so they are elliptical allowing the nozzle tubes to lie parallel against the cans side.
Step 3: Making a Pressure Vessel
Seal the top of the opened can using super glue and baking soda to make a small pressure vessel. Add some super glue to the closed opening and then sprinkle on some baking soda - they will combine to make a plastic. Keep adding super glue and baking soda until the top is sealed.
Step 4: Attaching the Nozzle Jets
Fit in the thin plastic tubes to the holes drilled in the sides of the can and seal with super glue and baking soda. Try to have the tubes pointing horizontal in the direction you want to rotate the can when the steam exits the nozzles.
Step 5: Creating Steam
Add a little water into the can though one of the nozzles. Just add maybe a teaspoon or so. 
Step 6: In Action
The can was suspended from a tripod over the methylated sprits flame. After a couple of minutes enough steam had built up to rotate the can.

Of course! Here's how to prepare Chewy Chocolate Chip Cookies:

Ingredients:

* 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
* 1/2 cup unsalted butter, softened
* 1 cup white granulated sugar
* 1/2 cup brown sugar
* 2 large eggs
* 2 teaspoons vanilla extract
* 1 cup semi-sweet chocolate chips
* 1/4 teaspoon salt

Steps:

1. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or a silicone mat.
2. In a medium-sized bowl, whisk together the flour, baking soda, and salt. Set aside.
3. In a large bowl, use an electric mixer to cream together the butter and sugars until light and fluffy, about 2-3 minutes.
4. Beat in the eggs one at a time, followed by the vanilla extract.
5. Gradually mix in the dry ingredients until just combined, being careful not to overmix.
6. Stir in the chocolate chips.
7. Scoop rounded tablespoonfuls of the dough onto the prepared baking sheet, leaving about 2 inches of space between each cookie.
8. Bake for 10-12 minutes or until the edges are lightly golden brown and the centers are set.
9. Remove the cookies from the oven and let them cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes before transferring them to a wire rack to cool completely.

That's it! Your Chewy Chocolate Chip Cookies are now ready to be enjoyed. Enjoy!

Ingredients:

* 3 ripe avocados
* 1/2 cup unsweetened cocoa powder
* 1/4 cup maple syrup
* 1/4 cup coconut cream
* 1/4 teaspoon salt
* 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract
* 1/4 cup chopped dark chocolate (at least 70% cocoa)

Instructions:

5. Refrigerate the mousse for at least 30 minutes to allow it to set.
6. Just before serving, top the mousse with chopped dark chocolate.
7. Enjoy!

The avocado adds a creamy texture and a subtle nutty flavor, while the cocoa powder provides a deep chocolate flavor. 1. Patrol and Monitoring: Conduct regular patrols of the premises on foot or by vehicle to prevent and detect signs of criminal activity, such as theft, vandalism, or trespassing. Monitor CCTV cameras and alarm systems to identify potential security breaches.
2. Access Control: Control and monitor access to the building, ensuring that only authorized personnel are allowed entry. This includes checking identification, controlling visitor access, and escorting visitors and contractors.
3. Incident Response: Respond promptly and effectively to security incidents, such as alarms, disturbances, or accidents. Assess the situation, take appropriate action, and notify the appropriate authorities as needed.
4. Crisis Management: Develop and implement crisis management plans to handle emergencies such as natural disasters, terrorist attacks, or other security threats. Participate in drills and training exercises to ensure readiness and preparedness.
5. Investigations: Conduct investigations into security incidents, including gathering evidence, interviewing witnesses, and preparing reports.
6. Training and Awareness: Provide security training and awareness programs for employees and visitors, including training on security procedures, emergency response plans, and the proper use of security equipment.
7. Reporting: Maintain accurate and detailed records of security incidents, including logs of patrols, alarms, and investigations. Prepare and submit regular reports to management and other stakeholders as required.
8. Communication: Maintain effective communication with other security personnel, management, and external agencies, including law enforcement and emergency services.
9. Compliance: Ensure compliance with relevant laws, regulations, and organizational policies, including those related to security, safety, and privacy.
10. Continuous Improvement: Stay up-to-date with the latest security trends, technologies, and best practices. Identify areas for improvement and make recommendations for enhancing the security posture of the organization.

context:
Paper: The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks that include an encoder and a decoder. The best performing models also connect the encoder and decoder through an attention mechanism. We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely. Experiments on two machine translation tasks show these models to be superior in quality while being more parallelizable and requiring significantly less time to train. Our model achieves 28.4 BLEU on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task, improving over the existing best results, including ensembles, by over 2 BLEU. On the WMT 2014 English-to-French translation task, our model establishes a new single-model state-of-the-art BLEU score of 41.8 after training for 3.5 days on eight GPUs, a small fraction of the training costs of the best models from the literature. We show that the Transformer generalizes well to other tasks by applying it successfully to English constituency parsing both with large and limited training data.

Of course! Here are some engaging and interactive activities or conversation starters that can help break the ice at meetups:

1. Two Truths and a Lie: Each person shares two true statements about themselves and one false statement. The other participants have to guess which one is the lie.
2. Human Bingo: Create bingo cards with different traits or characteristics, and have each person find someone who fits each square. When they find someone, they get to mark the square.
3. Speed Friending: Set up chairs in two rows facing each other, and have each person have two minutes to talk to the person opposite them. After two minutes, move one chair to the right and repeat.
4. Word Association Game: Have each person take turns saying a word, and the next person has to say a word that is associated with the previous word.
5. Would You Rather: Present a series of hypothetical situations and ask each person to choose which option they would prefer. For example, "Would you rather have the ability to fly or be invisible?"
6. Group Storytelling: Have each person start telling a story, and then pass it on to the next person, who continues the story, and so on.
7. Icebreaker Charades: Write down different words or phrases on slips of paper, and put them in a hat. Each person takes a turn drawing a slip of paper and acting out the word or phrase without speaking. The other participants have to guess what it is.
8. Scavenger Hunt: Create a list of items or challenges that can be found or completed around the meetup location, and have each person or team complete as many as they can.
9. Group Trivia: Create a trivia game with questions related to a particular topic or theme, and have each person or team compete to answer the most questions correctly.
10. The One-Word Game: Choose a word related to the meetup topic or theme, and have each person say only one word that comes to mind when they hear the word.

These activities are designed to be fun, interactive, and easy to facilitate, and can help break the ice and create a relaxed atmosphere at your meetup.

ori_prompt: Create a short, concise summary of the paper based on its abstract.
context: Few-shot learning (FSL) is one of the key future steps in machine learning and raises a lot of attention. In this paper, we focus on the FSL problem of dialogue understanding, which contains two closely related tasks: intent detection and slot filling. Dialogue understanding has been proven to benefit a lot from jointly learning the two sub-tasks. However, such joint learning becomes challenging in the few-shot scenarios: on the one hand, the sparsity of samples greatly magnifies the difficulty of modeling the connection between the two tasks; on the other hand, how to jointly learn multiple tasks in the few-shot setting is still less investigated. In response to this, we introduce FewJoint, the first FSL benchmark for joint dialogue understanding. FewJoint provides a new corpus with 59 different dialogue domains from real industrial API and a code platform to ease FSL experiment set-up, which are expected to advance the research of this field. Further, we find that insufficient performance of the few-shot setting often leads to noisy sharing between two sub-task and disturbs joint learning. To tackle this, we guide slot with explicit intent information and propose a novel trust gating mechanism that blocks low-confidence intent information to ensure high quality sharing. Besides, we introduce a Reptile-based meta-learning strategy to achieve better generalization in unseen few-shot domains. In the experiments, the proposed method brings significant improvements on two datasets and achieve new state-of-the-art performance.

Begin near the city of San Diego and make the first stop in coastal La Jolla. This upscale little village is a great a place for an overnight, a day of sunbathing at La Jolla Shores Beach, or a cocktail with a view.
Just 20 minutes north, stop into beachy Encinitas to window shop the boutiques or sample fish tacos. Walk through the coastal meditation garden at the Self-Realization Fellowship or join surfers in the line-up at one of the fantastic local beaches here
Just up the coast is cute little San Juan Capistrano, home to one of California’s favorite missions. In spring, more than 6,000 swallows migrate here from Argentina! As you approach LA, don’t miss swank Laguna Hills. Home to the one-of-a-kind Pageant of the Masters art event, Laguna is brimming with artists and charm. It’s a great place for an overnight. Plus, Crystal Cove Beach in nearby Newport Beach is one of California’s finest!
After that, the choice is yours: Disney lovers should head directly to Disneyland in Anaheim to meet Mickey. To join the beautiful people and snap a photo of an iconic California scene, head to Santa Monica Pier and walk the boardwalk or ride the world’s only solar-powered Ferris wheel. A San Diego to LA road trip is the perfect way to enjoy all things Southern California.

Kale and Almond Butter Stir-Fry with Apple Cider Vinegar and Agave Nectar Tamari Glaze

Ingredients:

* 2 cups kale, chopped
* 2 tablespoons almond butter
* 1/4 cup apple cider vinegar
* 2 tablespoons agave nectar
* 1 tablespoon tamari
* Salt and pepper to taste
* Cooking oil or avocado oil for frying

Instructions:

1. Heat a tablespoon of oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat.
2. Add the chopped kale and cook for 2-3 minutes, until it starts to soften.
3. Add the almond butter and stir to combine. Cook for another 2-3 minutes, until the kale is wilted and the almond butter is melted.
4. In a small bowl, whisk together the apple cider vinegar, agave nectar, and tamari. Pour the mixture over the kale and almond butter and stir to combine.
5. Cook for another minute, until the sauce has thickened slightly and the kale is coated in the glaze.
6. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
7. Serve hot, garnished with chopped nuts or seeds if desired.

Enjoy your delicious and healthy dinner!
